title: From Denoising Training to Test-Time Adaptation: Enhancing Domain Generalization for Medical Image Segmentation (DeY-Net / DeTTA)
mechanism: A U-Net is trained with an auxiliary denoising decoder on the shared encoder; at test time the encoder is adapted per sample with the denoising loss.
adaptation: Add a 1-channel denoising decoder to U-Net++ during the 20k-step house training, with Gaussian plus EL-like shot noise. Then run 10-step denoising TTT per cell (test) or per module (E1) on the encoder only.
min_experiment: Arm: house + joint denoising decoder (5 seeds), with and without TTT. Baselines: the same model without TTT, and the house model. Metrics: E1 relF1@2 and inactive IoU, test clean-49 guard. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.02 or the aux head alone costs > 0.005 crack IoU.
evidence: R: domain-generalisation gains on liver segmentation benchmarks over the baseline (exact numbers not retrieved).
prior_overlap: Partial. DDeP (decoder denoising pretraining on the pool, then fine-tune) was n.d., but that discards the aux head. Joint training with test-time use of the aux loss was never run.
